Univ. of Oklahoma expulsions infringe free speech rights, experts say | Al Jazeera America

The President of the university made the decision to expel the students based on the fact that their actions/words made the university an uncomfortable and/or hostile learning event for some students...something that is clearly outlined in the student handbook of every university.

Sure, you have free speech, but your words still have consequences.

I agree. I can go into work and say to a black colleague "Hey monkey nigger" and I would not be arrested but I would sure as fuck lose my job. Same if I said to my boss "I hate you, you are one smug bastard", not nearly as incendiary as racially abusing somebody but I would still get fired. It's all well and good that you have the right to say what you like, but to act as if your words will not have consequences is either naive or disingenuous.

But you can't be punished by standing on a town green and chanting "niggers go home!" Because this is a public university, and not private, certain constitutional protections do prevail. This is state-owned (i.e., public) land. The university covered it's ass by claiming that this interfered with the learning environment, which would be a reason for chucking someone out. However, they are on extremely thin ice.

While I think that these students were racist idiots, I am against lazy catch-all policies that allow people to be expelled every time an administrator feel public pressure. Literally anything can make someone "uncomfortable" or be interpreted as a "hostile environment" if someone is sensitive enough. The idea that a university is supposed to cater to everyone's comfort creates a ridiculous dynamic that will be impossible to objectively maintain the more people realize it can be weaponized.
